PLANNING COMMISSION
STAFF REPORT
Date: April 17, 2024
To: Reno City Planning Commission
Subject: Staff Report (For Possible Action): Case No. LDC24-00037 (Gentry
Conditional Use Permit) – A request has been made for a conditional use
permit to reestablish a discontinued, nonconforming outdoor storage use. The
±1.32 acre site is located on the north side of Gentry Way approximately ±135
feet east of its intersection with South Virginia Street (85 Gentry Way). The
site is located in the Mixed-Use Urban (MU) zoning district and has a Master
Plan land use designation of Urban Mixed-Use (UMU).
From: Leah Piccotti, Associate Planner
Ward #: 1
Case No.: LDC24-00037 (Gentry Conditional Use Permit)
Applicant: Raven’s Wing Limited LLC
APN: 020-182-13
Request: Conditional Use Permit: To reestablish a previously existing,
nonconforming outdoor storage use.
Location: See Case Maps (Exhibit A)
Proposed Motion: Based upon compliance with the applicable findings, I move to approve
the conditional use permit, subject to the conditions listed in the staff
report.
Summary: The proposed conditional use permit would allow for the reestablishment of
nonconforming outdoor storage use on a portion of a ±1.32 acre site. The property is located in the
Mixed-Use Urban (MU) zoning district. Outdoor storage is only permitted in the MU zoning
district in designated areas; this site is outside of those designated areas. The nonconforming use
was extinguished approximately 20 years ago. If a nonconforming use ceases operation for a period
longer than one year, a conditional use permit (CUP) may be used to reestablish the use. Key
project issues include: 1) overall site design; 2) compatibility with surrounding land uses; 3)
conformance with Reno Municipal Code (RMC); and 4) conformance with the ReImagine Reno
1
Master Plan. Staff can make all of the findings and recommends approval of the conditional use
permit, on a temporary basis, subject to the conditions of approval in the staff report.
Background: Under the previous code, adopted prior to 2021, this area was located in the
Community Commercial (CC) zoning district. CC zoning was intended to provide general
commercial and service enterprises for the community at large. Outdoor storage was not allowed
in the previous zoning district and it is unclear when the outdoor storage use was established. Staff
found that the site has been used commercially since 1974 when a building permit for an “electric
sign” was issued. However, business licenses were not required until the mid 1980’s. The earliest
record of a business license issued at the site is for an interior design business in 1990.
Historical aerial images of the site (Exhibit B) depict vehicles and shipping containers stored on
the site beginning between 1994 and 1999. This corresponds with the business license for
Marathon Co., described on the license as “moving assistance; packing, loading, offloading.” Prior
to Marathon Co., Al’s Moving Company and Jones Packing and Loading were licensed on the
parcel and assumed to include outdoor storage use as accessory. Although moving companies do
not meet the definition of Outdoor Storage, it is not uncommon for them to have outdoor yard
areas for the storage of trucks, containers, etc. This is consistent with the historic aerial images of
the site. Other documented land uses established on the site include automobile rental (Reno Truck
Rental), a party rental agency, general laborer, and interior design services. A communications
facility (cell tower) was legally established at the site in 2001.At that time, the associated
application stated that the existing land use was “Uhaul Storage Facility”.
Beginning in 2020, Snow Lion moved heavy equipment onto the parcel without a business license.
In March of 2023, the Business License Compliance Division notified the property owner that a
business license was required for storage of the equipment. In April 2023, Snow Lion applied for
a business license, describing the operations as “snow and ice removal equipment storage—
outdoor storage.” The business license for Snow Lion was denied because Staff was unable to
determine whether outdoor storage was ever legally established on the site. The burden of
demonstrating the lawful establishment of a nonconformity is on the owner of property per RMC
Section 18.01.402(d). Based on submitted materials and the recent research previously noted,
including historical aerial images. staff determined that there is sufficient evidence and
justification to permit the reestablishment of outdoor storage, subject to the approval of a CUP.
Discussion: Outdoor storage is defined as Property used for the long term (more than 72 hours)
retention of materials, machinery, large vehicles, including boats and recreational vehicles,
and/or equipment; regardless of whether materials, machinery, large vehicles, or equipment are
to be bought, sold, repaired, stored, incinerated, or discarded. New or used motor vehicle sales
and rental display and parking shall not be defined as outside storage if the vehicles are operable.
(RMC 18.09.305 Industrial Uses).
2
1
9
8
7
Per RMC 18.01.403(a), a non-conforming use that was legally established prior to the effective
date of this Title or subsequent amendments thereto without a conditional use permit or other
entitlement is deemed to have a conditional use permit or other entitlement. Per RMC 18.01.403(f),
a nonconforming use that is abandoned or discontinued for a period of one year or more may only
be resumed with a conditional use permit reviewed by the Planning Commission. In this case,
historical images demonstrate outdoor storage on the parcel from approximately 1999 to 2017.
The application for the onsite wireless communication facility approved in 2001 states the parcel
was used as a storage facility. Land uses between 1974 and 1990 are undocumented.
Analysis:
Overall Site Design: The site is developed with a single-family residence, built in 1964, and a
wireless communication facility, both located at the north end of the parcel. A paved parking area
is located on the south end, adjacent to Gentry Way. With exception of the parking area, the site
is fully fenced with a 6-foot chain-link fence. The proposed ±15,632 square foot outdoor storage
area will be located directly behind the fence, south of the onsite residence (Exhibit C).
Staff recommends the outdoor storage area be restricted to the ±15,632 square foot area depicted
on the site plan (Condition No. 5). An existing access easement for the wireless communication
facility shall be maintained for access to both the wireless communication facility and the existing
residence (Condition No. 6). Existing shipping containers shall be permitted (Condition No. 7).
The proposed outdoor storage area is currently paved but is extremely deteriorated. To reduce air
and water pollution, soil erosion, and street sweeping costs, all existing deteriorated/unpaved areas
used for driving, off-street parking, or storage of vehicles/equipment shall be paved with asphalt
and/or concrete (Condition No. 8). Additionally, a parking area striping plan shall be submitted
demonstrating that the parking lot, outside of the fence, meets minimum RMC parking lot design
requirements (Condition No. 9). Landscaping along Gentry Way, including Irrigation, shall be
reestablished/rehabilitated and maintained (Condition No. 10). The hours and days of construction
shall be limited to mitigate the impact on residents of the adjacent multi-family residential complex
(Condition No. 11).
There is a monument sign on the parcel for Ryder/Budget Rental Truck, which has been out of
business since 2006. Per RMC 18.05.112 any sign or sign structure which has been abandoned
for a period of six months shall be removed or restored to use within 30 days after a notice of
abandonment is issued by the Administrator to the owner of the sign. The sign shall be removed
or restored within 30 days of a decision by the Planning Commission (Condition No. 12).
Compatibility with Surrounding Uses: Adjacent to the west, fronting South Virginia Street, is a
market and two automobile repair businesses. To the east is a 47-unit apartment complex. To the
north is a vacant parcel and to the south, across Gentry Way, is a fast-food restaurant and an auto
3
1
9
8
7
repair shop. Uses in the general area are typical of a mixed-use area; apartment complexes, mobile
home parks, restaurants, retail, and automobile sales and services. Newer development in this area
has been primarily multi-family residential, including a 208 unit apartment complex developed in
2021 (further east along Gentry Way).
Staff recommends screening the site from South Virginia Street, as it may be visible through the
adjacent parking areas, as well as screening on the east to mitigate potential impacts on the adjacent
apartment complex. The applicant has proposed installing slats in the existing chain link fence
with a five-foot-wide landscaping buffer and a dense evergreen hedge, five feet in height at the
time of planting (Condition No. 13).
Conformance with Reno Municipal Code: The MU district is intended to promote an urban
pattern of mixed-use development. The MU district is located adjacent to existing/planned high-
frequency transit corridors, or where higher pedestrian activity is desired. The district
accommodates an integrated mix of higher-density residential, commercial, retail, employment,
and other service-oriented uses, with higher-intensity uses located adjacent to designated Urban
Corridors. The site is located in an Urban Corridor and higher intensity uses exist, such as
automotive service and sales. Outdoor storage is permitted in the MU zoning district in designated
areas. Exhibit D includes the RMC Table of Allowed Uses identifying the limited zoning districts
that allow outdoor storage, the associated outdoor storage use standards, and a map depicting the
locations where outdoor storage is permitted within the MU zoning district.
RMC 18.03.306(b)(3) requires that outdoor storage be located to the side or rear of the principal
building and screened from adjacent roadways, parks, and residential zoned property within 750
feet of the use with landscaping and a solid fence no shorter than the allowed storage height. Due
to existing configuration of the site, the outdoor storage cannot be located to the side or rear of the
principal building and, therefore, cannot meet the applicable development standards. This is an
existing nonconformity that may be permitted with the approval of the CUP to reestablish the
discontinued outdoor storage use.
The area surrounding the site has changed substantially since the site was developed in 1964 and
continues to evolve with new development; primarily multi-family complexes and commercial
uses. Properties in the immediate vicinity of the site are primarily multi-family residential and
automotive repair and sales. While new or used motor vehicle sales and rental display parking is
not defined as outside storage, the outdoor storage of heavy equipment may be considered
reasonably compatible, on a temporary basis. As the Urban Corridor is redeveloped, it is
anticipated that more residential units will be added and the area will trend toward accommodating
the integral mix of residential, commercial, retail, employment, and other service-oriented uses, as
intended in the MU zoning district. Permanently allowing industrial use (outdoor storage) in this
area may not be appropriate. However, a temporary entitlement (maximum of five years) may be

considered reasonably compatible with the types of uses permitted in the area (Condition No. 14).
Should this request be approved, Staff recommends that no extension of this conditional use permit
be issued beyond the five year timeframe. After a period of five years the nonconforming use shall
be permanently extinguished.
Master Plan Conformance: The subject site has a Master Plan land use designation of Urban
Mixed-Use (UMU) and is located in a Mixed-Use Area per the Structure Plan Framework of the
Reno Master Plan. The Urban Mixed-Use land use designation supports a range of commercial,
retail, employment, and service-oriented uses to serve adjacent neighborhoods and the broader
community. Secondary uses include medium to high-density residential uses, civic and
government uses, as well as public spaces and other community oriented uses. In addition, the site
is located in an Urban Corridor and between two regional centers. Urban corridors are multimodal
in character and encourage a mix of higher-density residential, retail, commercial, and other
employment and service-oriented uses, especially within ¼ mile of transit stations.
Staff analysis of the UMU land use designation, and guiding principles finds that nonconforming
nonresidential uses are generally not supported by master plan policies in the urban corridor. Per
the Structure Plan framework the site is located in a mixed-use area, in an urban corridor, and
located between the two city centers; Downtown and the Convention Center. Urban corridor area
specific policies focus on design standards. Conditions 8, 9, 12, and 13 will enhance site aesthetics
and bring the property into closer compliance with current RMC standards, encouraging adaptive
reuse of the site upon cessation of the outdoor storage in five years. This includes significant
screening, landscaping, and overall site improvements. The streetscape improvements and future
adaptive reuse of the site are consistent with Master Plan goals and objectives.
The Master Plan does include policies that support reestablishment of the use on a temporary (five
year) basis. Guiding Principal (GP) 1 encourages a resilient local and regional economy. GP 1.4
supports the growth, creation, and retention of local businesses and start-ups. GP 1.4A encourages
Staff to continue to identify new ways to reduce barriers to entry and streamline licensing
frameworks for new businesses. In this case, Staff has recommended the conditional use permit be
temporary, allowing the business to continue operation and provide ample time to transition to a
new facility/location.
Public and Stakeholder Engagement: The project was reviewed by various City divisions and
partner agencies. Courtesy notices and hearing notices were sent out to surrounding property
owners and no comments have been received. The request was scheduled for both the February
and March Ward 1 Neighborhood Advisory Board (NAB) meetings. Both meetings were canceled.
Project information was forwarded to NAB members and no comments were provided. Any future
comments will be forwarded to the Planning Commission.

Development Services Department staff, unless otherwise noted.
